prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production creature concept reference for an original futuristic ocean hover-racing game, to be modeled and animated in Blender.
Primary request: ONE enormous aquatic worm, around 180 metres long, swimming out of a stormy teal ocean, breaching in a huge graceful arch OVER a narrow elevated race track, then diving back into the sea. Awe and scale, not a boss fight.
Subject: one continuous long muscular eel/worm silhouette with a blunt elegant wedge-shaped head, small luminous eyes, tapered tail, subtle overlapping pearl-grey segmented dorsal plates, dark teal wet skin, fine cyan bioluminescent seams and a flowing low fin ridge. Animal anatomy, no limbs, no wings, no dragon horns, no teeth display. Make the head and the continuous body silhouette very clear for a 3D modeler.
Scene: alien ocean under storm clouds; sleek white ceramic and dark teal race track about 30 metres wide with cyan edge lights. A single tiny seven-metre hovercraft is on the track to establish immense scale. The animal arches well above the track, with its trailing lower body and tail entering the water on the opposite side; water streams off the belly and fins, immense foam disturbance at the ocean contact.
Style: polished cinematic game concept painting with believable volumetric 3D forms and crisp readable silhouette, restrained materials, beautiful pearl/teal palette. Cool overcast daylight with a bright opening in the storm clouds, enough fill light to read the dark body.
Composition: one wide landscape hero view, three-quarter side view from slightly above track level. Whole creature in frame with comfortable margins, one coherent animal crossing from one side of the road to the other. Keep the road visibly open beneath the arch. No inset views, no labels, no text, no watermark, no extra creatures.
purpose: Original Nacre Tempest leviathan concept and Blender reference; not a runtime texture.
